There are many different roads to the same broad conclusion, and I think that if you took it seriously the leftist analysis of American politics ALSO leads to the conclusion that Democrats need a narrower policy agenda.

slowboring.com/p/most-politi…

A slightly separate issue is that I kind of agree with Trump that *official buildings* should use neoclassical architecture because of the specific symbolism that plays in the tradition of the American republic (plus they look nice).

A lot of aspects of current building codes, parking, weird fire department hangups, and even design review seem to explicitly nudge buildings uglier and we definitely shouldn’t do that. 

But I think the core issues here are the growth benefit of clear property rights.

Nice looking buildings > ugly buildings and if there are reasonable measures to encourage more beautiful buildings I am all for it, but I worry “YIMBY but only for nice buildings” is becoming a new version of “I’d be all for it if only the housing were ‘affordable.’”
